_comment: One of the nine plain colours, and it sets every colour there is to set.
`colour` is one name on five aspects -- the star this world goes round, the curtain over its cold, the
bow opposite its sun, and the grass and the leaves that grow in it. Each of those holds exactly one
colour, so the name needs no prefix and attachment decides which is meant. The vault, the air and the
cloud are still named outright, because the sky and the air each hold two colours and something has to
It declares no aspects: `Word.aspects` is widened from the parameters a word sets, so the `sets` map is
the whole of the declaration. `red sky` paints the vault, `red sun` the star, `red and green aurora`
the ramp from its crown to its hem, and `a red Age` means all of them at once.
The light is deliberately *not* among them. Saying the light here is red is a different claim from
saying the sky is, and `witchlight` is the idiom that already makes it.
These replaced `crimson`, `emerald` and `violet`, and retired `verdigris` -- which was `sky: green` and
nothing else, which is `green sky` said in a word a writer has to learn first (Jonah, 2026-08-29).
